description: Experience the ultimate balance of bold flavors with this classic Hot and Sour Soup, a beloved staple of Chinese cuisine. Each spoonful delivers a tantalizing blend of spicy heat from white pepper, tangy notes from rice vinegar, and savory depth from broth and mushrooms. This comforting soup, packed with tender pork, silky tofu, and crunchy bamboo shoots, is perfect for warming you from the inside out.

ingredients.notes: drained and cut into small strips
mixed with 3 tbsp cold water to form a slurry
black vinegar can be used for deeper flavor

instructions.title: Prepare Ingredients
instructions.text: Rehydrate dried shiitake and wood ear mushrooms in hot water for 20 minutes, then drain, squeeze dry, remove shiitake stems, and thinly slice both types. Thinly slice the pork, tofu, and bamboo shoots. Beat the eggs in a small bowl and set aside. Prepare the cornstarch slurry by mixing cornstarch with cold water.

instructions.title: Simmer Broth and Pork
instructions.text: Pour the chicken or vegetable broth into a large pot and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Add the thinly sliced pork and cook for 2-3 minutes until it is no longer pink. Skim any foam that rises to the surface.

instructions.title: Add Vegetables and Tofu
instructions.text: Once the pork is cooked, add the sliced shiitake mushrooms, wood ear mushrooms, and bamboo shoots to the broth. Bring the soup back to a gentle simmer and cook for another 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.

instructions.title: Season the Soup
instructions.text: Stir in the soy sauce, rice vinegar, and white pepper. Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed, adding more vinegar for tang or white pepper for heat. If desired, add chili oil at this stage for an extra layer of spice.

instructions.title: Thicken and Add Egg
instructions.text: Stir the cornstarch slurry once more, then slowly pour it into the simmering soup while continuously stirring to prevent lumps. Cook for 1-2 minutes until the soup thickens to your desired consistency. Reduce heat to low, then slowly drizzle the beaten eggs into the soup in a thin stream, stirring gently in one direction to create delicate egg ribbons.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the soup from the heat. Stir in the sesame oil. Ladle the hot and sour soup into individual bowls and garnish generously with sliced green onions before serving immediately. Enjoy this comforting and flavorful Chinese classic.

tips: For truly authentic flavor, use Chinkiang black vinegar instead of regular rice vinegar. Its deeper, slightly sweeter notes add complexity.
Adjust the amount of white pepper and rice vinegar to your personal preference for 'hot' and 'sour'. Some prefer more of one than the other.
To achieve delicate egg ribbons, pour the beaten egg slowly into the simmering soup while stirring continuously in a circular motion, then stop stirring and let it set for a moment before serving.
